title: tennessee-lpm Policy Controversy Record
description: A new record type, first authored in this repo (2026-10-20) and intended as a shared ecosystem-wide addition alongside deutsche_lp/nys_lp/india-lpm's existing nine schemas -- a bounded, named public dispute over curriculum policy, with multiple named actors taking opposing or differing positions, real media coverage, and a tracked resolution (or lack of one). None of the existing nine record types model this directly: policy-timeline-event records a single dated fact, institutional-mandate-record records a single authority's requirement, and coherence-finding-record records a textual comparison -- but a real controversy (the 2008 Florida evolution-wording fight, the 2026 proposed-standards fight) is made of many of those, held together by contested stakes, named sides, and press coverage, which is exactly the 'politics' dimension this repo was built to capture. A policy-controversy-record does not duplicate the text of its own timeline events or mandates -- it POINTS at them (via contestedObjects' relatedEventIds/relatedMandateIds) and adds the layer those schemas don't carry: who took which side, what the press said, and whether a recurring fault line connects this episode to an earlier or later one.

id.description: Provisional, repo-local id. See GOVERNANCE.md. A sibling repo adopting this schema uses its own prefix (e.g. NYLP-CONTROVERSY-, INLP-CONTROVERSY-, DELP-CONTROVERSY-).

controversyType.description: 'standards-adoption-fight' = a dispute over a governing board's vote to adopt/readopt a standards document (e.g. the 2008 NGSSS 4-3 vote, a 2026 State Board vote). 'curriculum-content-dispute' = a dispute over what specific content should say, short of a formal adoption vote (e.g. public comment on a draft). 'textbook-or-materials-challenge' = a dispute over a specific instructional material, often under a named objection process (e.g. Florida's 2017 instructional-materials-objection statute). 'legislative-mandate-fight' = a dispute over a bill before it becomes a mandate (track the bill itself via a policy-timeline-event with eventType 'legislation'; this record is for the surrounding public fight). 'personnel-or-appointment-fight' = a dispute centered on who holds a decision-making role (e.g. a contested State Board appointment). 'litigation' = a dispute that became or stemmed from a lawsuit.

topicArea.description: The specific curricular content at stake, in plain language, e.g. 'explicit naming of evolution and natural selection in high-school biology standards'. Not the same as controversyType, which is about the dispute's institutional shape.

summary.description: Two or three sentences stating what the controversy was actually about and why -- plain language, no jargon, written so it stands on its own without reading the linked records.

dateEnd.description: Omit if unresolved/ongoing as of this record's provenance.date.

status.description: 'emerging' = surfacing, not yet a full public fight. 'active' = genuinely in progress as of provenance.date. 'resolved-outcome-adopted' = the change the controversy was fought over went into effect. 'resolved-outcome-rejected' = the change did not happen / the status quo held. 'resolved-compromise' = neither side's full position prevailed (e.g. the 2008 'scientific theory of evolution' wording, which satisfied neither side completely). 'dormant-unresolved' = no longer active but never formally resolved either way. 'recurring' = this specific episode resolved, but recurrenceOf/recurrenceContinuedBy below chain it to a pattern that resurfaces across years -- use alongside one of the resolved-* values, not instead of one, once this episode itself has concluded.

outcomeSummary.description: What actually happened, in plain language. Required once status is any resolved-* or dormant-unresolved value; may be omitted while status is emerging/active.

recurrenceOf.description: Ids of earlier policy-controversy-records this episode is a recurrence/continuation of -- the same underlying fault line resurfacing (e.g. a 2026 standards fight that revisits the exact same wording question the 2008 fight already fought over). This is the field that turns several disconnected episodes into one documented, decades-long pattern -- the core of 'historically' documenting a region's curriculum politics, not just cataloguing isolated incidents.

recurrenceContinuedBy.description: Ids of later policy-controversy-records that continue this episode's fault line. Usually left for the LATER record's own recurrenceOf to populate instead (avoiding the same link stated twice in two places) -- populate here only if this record is edited after a later episode already exists and the later record's own file is not being touched in the same change.

crossRepoRefs.description: Added 2026-10-20 alongside institutional-actor-record's identical field: ids of a controversy in a SIBLING repo that is part of the same broader national or cross-jurisdiction pattern as this one, without being the same recurring fault line in the stricter recurrenceOf sense (recurrenceOf is reserved for the same jurisdiction's own fault line resurfacing; crossRepoRefs is for a different jurisdiction's own, separately-adjudicated episode that nonetheless belongs to the same larger story -- e.g. a national-level 'American evolution-education culture war' controversy record pointing at each state repo's own controversy records). Deliberately free-text, not a validated cross-repo link -- same informal-reference discipline this ecosystem already uses for ConceptBase/CompetencyBase ids. Format: '<repo>:<that repo's own controversy id>', e.g. 'tennessee-lpm:TNLP-CONTROVERSY-butler-act-and-scopes-trial'.

contestedObjects.description: The actual policy/standard content at stake, pointing at existing records rather than re-quoting their text.

positions.description: Who took which side, and what they actually said -- the heart of documenting the politics, not just the policy outcome.

actorId.description: Optional link to an institutional-actor-record, where the actor is already modeled there.

actorLabel.description: Free-text name, always required even when actorId is also given -- a position entry must be readable on its own without resolving a cross-reference. Use this alone for a named individual (a legislator, a board member) not modeled as their own institutional-actor-record.

stanceSummary.description: What this actor actually said or did, in plain language -- a real position, not a label. Prefer a short, bounded, attributed quotation where one exists in the source (see sourceUrl/accessTier).

accessTier.description: Governs stanceSummary where it contains a direct quotation. Same four values and meaning as this repo's other schemas' identical field.

mediaCoverage.description: Real, named press/media coverage of this controversy -- optional but strongly expected for any well-documented US public controversy, since press coverage is often the only record of how a dispute was actually framed to the public.

framingNote.description: Optional: how this outlet characterized the controversy, if notable (e.g. a local outlet framing it as a parents'-rights issue vs. a science-education outlet framing it as a standards-rigor issue). A factual observation about framing, not this repo's own editorializing.

quotedExcerpt.description: A short, bounded direct quotation from the article, if used. Governed by accessTier below -- news reporting is copyrighted; keep this short and clearly attributed.

accessTier.description: Governs quotedExcerpt. 'citation-only' (headline + url, no quotedExcerpt) is the safe default for third-party journalism; raise to 'excerpt-only' only for a short, clearly-bounded, attributed quotation.

themes.description: Open string list for cross-controversy querying, e.g. ['evolution', 'academic-freedom-legislation', 'standards-adoption'].

exhaustivenessCaveat.description: Explicit statement of how exhaustive the underlying search was -- required honesty, same convention as coherence-finding-record.
